hints: There are at most 2^20 ways to choose one group, which is small enough to examine.
For each subset, add its apple weights and compare its sum with the remaining total.
Track the smallest absolute difference; choosing a subset automatically leaves the other apples in the second group.
analogy: Try every possible assignment of each apple to the first group; the rest form the second group.
example: For weights 3,2,7,4,1, choosing 2,3,4 gives 9 and the remainder 8, so the difference is 1.
algorithm: Enumerate every subset (for example, bit masks), sum its weights, and minimize abs(total-2*subsetSum).
correctness: Every division corresponds to a subset and its complement; evaluating all subsets therefore includes an optimal division.
complexity: O(n*2^n) time with direct summation (or O(2^n) incremental subset sums) and O(1) extra space.
